source_text: I'd like to pause here and mention that when codex-19 was working on verifying their transpiled Lisp code, they were finding various problems with it. For the moment, we're just trying to build a transpiler, but the earlier experiments with codex-19 was suggesting that for whatever reason it wasn't working out for them.  I don't know if adding more and more language features will help with that.  I don't know if we could potentially verify *in Lean* that our transpiler is actually correct, but that would be an interesting touch, i.e., back-translating the transpiler into provable claims about the transpiler and then proving them

㊥ (concrete investigation) Paused feature expansion and committed `3e026ef`: a reproducible check of Codex-19’s historical class-key failure.

㊬ (result) The same generated program fails on runtime `61d631b` with the recorded hashing refusal and passes on the current committed runtime. This confirms one runtime repair—not whole-program correctness. [Evidence and proof obligations](/home/joe/code/mfuton-sbcl/lisp/transpiler/evidence/class-key-failure-replay.json).

㊭ (Lean direction) This gives us a concrete candidate: prove preservation of class identity and dictionary lookup/update behavior. The proof must connect to the actual generated operations and runtime implementation.

㊟ (limits) No Lean proof was produced this turn, and the full failing application was not replayed.
